description: ARRAY_SORT(array [, sort_ascending [, nulls_first]]). Ascending by default, descending when sort_ascending is FALSE. The two kinds of null behave differently, all live-verified: a SQL NULL array ELEMENT is the VARIANT undefined, and nulls_first (default FALSE for ascending order) moves it, so ARRAY_SORT([2,NULL,1]) is [1,2,undefined] while the same call with TRUE, TRUE is [undefined,1,2]. A JSON null is a VALUE ranked above every other variant type and nulls_first does NOT move it - ARRAY_SORT(PARSE_JSON('[2,null,1]')) is [1,2,null] with or without nulls_first, and descending is [null,2,1]. With both present the order is [1,2,null,undefined]. The ranking is by variant type, not lexical: ARRAY_SORT(['z', PARSE_JSON('null')]) is ["z",null], which a text comparison of "null" would have put first, and a number sorts below an object which sorts below a JSON null. Converted 1:1 from functions/ArraySortTest (now retired); the array cells are read through TO_JSON so the assertion is on the array's JSON text rather than on a transport's own rendering of an ARRAY cell.

steps.sql: SELECT TO_JSON(ARRAY_SORT(ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(2, NULL, PARSE_JSON('null'), 1), TRUE, TRUE))
